pr.body:
closes #37118

PR is adding some context information to be available in the `access-token` without a need to introduce any additional custom claims. So far, it provides info about:

- session type (online, offline, transient), which was used to create the token
- token type (regular or lightweight token)
- grant type

These informations can be useful when token is later sent to some Keycloak endpoints (for example introspection, userInfo, admin/account REST API) to optimize something. For example:
- session-type will allow to lookup only correct session type based on the type of the session, which token was created from. As for example today, we need to lookup "online" session and if it is not found, then fallback to "offline" session. So possible unnecessary lookup. Related follow-up issue for optimize that: #37662

- Grant type knowledge can be useful for example for the token-exchange use-case: #37117

- Lightweight access token: We will be able to recognize more reliably if access-token is lightweight or not and do something based on that (EG. lookup roles from model instead of lookup roles from the token)

In this PR, I've made token ID to look something like `onrtac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The first 2 characters is shortcut for "session type" - `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for "token type" - `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The next 2 characters is shortcut for grant type - `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

Shortcuts are used, so the token ID contains important info, but at the same time, it is limited in size and does not introduce much new characters to the token.

The encoding into ID is used only for access-tokens. Not used for refresh tokens or ID tokens or any others.

Introduced dedicated SPI in the end. Wanted to "cache" some objects (EG. shortcuts for grant types etc) and it seems clearer to me to cache them at the level of factory, rather than in the static fields, which is not very pretty. Moreover, provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider (and eventually encode some more info or encode stuff in the different way etc).

#### Note

I've used 2 commits in this PR. Originally, in the 1st commit, I've made the encoding a bit longer with token ID to look something like `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:1f65761e-1c69-40a2-82da-2d8aa5e39a8a` .
  - The `st` is shortcut for "session type" and `on` is shortcut for "online" session
  - The `tt` is shortcut for "token type" and `rt` is shortcut for regular token (not lightweight token)
  - The `gt` is shortcut for grant type and `ac` is shortcut for "authorization code" grant

But assuming that every "type" has always 2 characters long shortcut, I've rather updated it in the 2nd commit to have only 7 new characters instead of 18 characters. I planned to squash before merge (unless you think that we should rather use longer format for some reason, in which case the 2nd commit can be removed from the PR).

raw_findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider finds no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute and encodes the grant shortcut as "na", so client-credentials access tokens carry an 'unknown' grant type even though ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory declares the shortcut "cc".
raw_findings.failure_mode: Encoded token context is incomplete for a supported grant, defeating the feature's purpose for that flow.
raw_findings.impact: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider finds no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute and encodes the grant shortcut as "na", so client-credentials access tokens carry an 'unknown' grant type even though ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory declares the shortcut "cc".
raw_findings.root_cause: The grant-type attribute is only populated in the shared createTokenResponse() helper, which the client-credentials (and UMA permission) grant does not use.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) in ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() (after attachAuthenticationSession) as done for the other grant paths.
raw_findings.title: client_credentials grant type is never recorded in the client session context
raw_findings.trigger: A token request with grant_type=client_credentials; ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() builds the response directly via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never calls createTokenResponse().

validated_findings.body: The matcher compares characters at index 3-4 ("ta" for "onrtac") instead of the grant shortcut at index 4-5 ("ac"), so the expected grant type is never actually verified by the assertion.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Assertions silently pass regardless of the grant encoded in the token id, providing no regression coverage.
validated_findings.impact: The matcher compares characters at index 3-4 ("ta" for "onrtac") instead of the grant shortcut at index 4-5 ("ac"), so the expected grant type is never actually verified by the assertion.
validated_findings.root_cause: Off-by-one indexing of the fixed 6-character encoded context introduced with the new matcher.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use items[0].substring(4, 6) to extract the grant shortcut (session type 0-1, token type 2-3, grant type 4-5).
validated_findings.title: isAccessTokenId reads the wrong characters for the grant shortcut
validated_findings.trigger: Any AssertEvents expectation using isAccessTokenId(), e.g. expectCodeToToken() matching a token id like "onrtac:<uuid>".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about off-by-one indexing is incorrect. Looking at the encoding format (session type 0-1, token type 2-3, grant type 4-5), substring(3,5) extracts characters at indices 3 and 4, which is indeed off by one from the grant shortcut at 4-5. However, the real bug is the inverted logic (equals returns false), not the index. This finding conflates two issues incorrectly.

validated_findings.body: The matcher rejects ids whose extracted shortcut equals the expected one and accepts all others, i.e. the grant-type check is logically reversed and cannot detect a wrong grant shortcut.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Test matcher asserts the opposite of the intended contract, so token-id encoding regressions go undetected.
validated_findings.impact: The matcher rejects ids whose extracted shortcut equals the expected one and accepts all others, i.e. the grant-type check is logically reversed and cannot detect a wrong grant shortcut.
validated_findings.root_cause: Missing negation when converting the equality check into an early-return guard.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Negate the condition: if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
validated_findings.title: isAccessTokenId inverts the grant shortcut comparison
validated_findings.trigger: Running any test that uses expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken with the new matcher.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 483 shows 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;' - when the shortcut matches, it returns false (rejecting the match). The logic is inverted: it should return false when NOT equal. Additionally substring(3,5) should be (4,6) per the 6-char prefix format.

validated_findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider finds no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute and encodes the grant shortcut as "na", so client-credentials access tokens carry an 'unknown' grant type even though ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory declares the shortcut "cc".
validated_findings.failure_mode: Encoded token context is incomplete for a supported grant, defeating the feature's purpose for that flow.
validated_findings.impact: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider finds no Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute and encodes the grant shortcut as "na", so client-credentials access tokens carry an 'unknown' grant type even though ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory declares the shortcut "cc".
validated_findings.root_cause: The grant-type attribute is only populated in the shared createTokenResponse() helper, which the client-credentials (and UMA permission) grant does not use.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType()) in ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() (after attachAuthenticationSession) as done for the other grant paths.
validated_findings.title: client_credentials grant type is never recorded in the client session context
validated_findings.trigger: A token request with grant_type=client_credentials; ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() builds the response directly via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never calls createTokenResponse().
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Repository context shows ClientCredentialsGrantType.java L140-141 calls tokenManager.responseBuilder().generateAccessToken() directly without calling createTokenResponse(). The setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE) is only in createTokenResponse() at line 109 of OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java, so client_credentials tokens won't have the grant type attribute set.

validated_findings.body: Documented contract contradicts the implementation (all in-tree shortcuts are 2 chars, decoding asserts a 6-char prefix), leading implementors to produce token ids that cannot be decoded.
validated_findings.evidence:
* @return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants. It can be useful for example in the tokens when the amount of characters should be limited and hence using full grant name
     * is not ideal. Shortcut should be unique across grants.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Misleading SPI documentation causes non-conforming implementations and runtime IllegalArgumentException on decode.
validated_findings.impact: Documented contract contradicts the implementation (all in-tree shortcuts are 2 chars, decoding asserts a 6-char prefix), leading implementors to produce token ids that cannot be decoded.
validated_findings.root_cause: Javadoc was written for the earlier variable-length encoding and not updated when the format was fixed to 2-character segments.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Correct the javadoc to state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique, matching the fixed-width encoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.
validated_findings.title: getShortcut() javadoc says 3 letters while the encoder requires exactly 2
validated_findings.trigger: An implementor follows the javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider then encodes a 7-character context prefix and getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects it with "Expected length of 6.".
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 29-31 state 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but all in-tree implementations use 2-character shortcuts (ac, cc, ro, etc.) and the decoder expects exactly 6 characters for the prefix. The javadoc is misleading and will cause implementors to create non-conforming shortcuts.

validated_findings.body: The token id is written with a context prefix of unexpected length and every later getTokenContextFromTokenId() call on that token throws IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6"), breaking introspection/userInfo consumers of the context.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unvalidated provider input produces token ids that the same provider cannot parse back.
validated_findings.impact: The token id is written with a context prefix of unexpected length and every later getTokenContextFromTokenId() call on that token throws IllegalArgumentException("Expected length of 6"), breaking introspection/userInfo consumers of the context.
validated_findings.root_cause: The fixed-width encoding assumption is enforced only on the decode side, never on the encode/registration side.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Validate grantShort.length() == 2 (ideally when registering shortcuts in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit) and fail fast with a descriptive error.
validated_findings.title: Missing length validation for grant shortcuts when encoding token ids
validated_findings.trigger: A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut whose length is not 2 (the javadoc even suggests 3 letters); an access token is then issued for that grant.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding claims missing length validation causes decode failures, but the encode side at line 109-112 throws IllegalStateException if grantShort is null. The actual issue is that non-2-char shortcuts would produce malformed tokens, but this is speculative without evidence of actual validation gap - the javadoc issue (candidate 5) is the root cause.
